subject: Bridging invoice ladder & provisional credit cap discussion
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmehealth.eu>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Ross <elena.ross@acmehealth.eu>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Request: move to Net60 for pilot + temporary invoice ladder

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency numbers. Finance at Acme is asking if we can move our initial invoices onto a temporary payment ladder while we complete an internal procurement review.

Concretely: would Redwood consider Net60 for the first three invoices (pilot month + two post-pilot months) while we run our security & procurement checks? If not Net60, would you accept Net45 with a 25% upfront deposit on month 1?

Also — because we operate across EU entities, our billing team needs EU VAT invoices (reverse-charge applicable). Can you confirm Redwood can issue VAT-detailed invoices to Acme Health Systems (VAT ID: EU123456789)?

I can share our credit application if needed. Please let me know what paperwork you require and a ballpark credit cap so our procurement can sign off.

Best,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Digital Ops | Acme Health Systems
oliver.grant@acmehealth.eu

--
Note: cc'ing Ben from Redwood since he was on the call and may have flex on billing cadence.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmehealth.eu>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: move to Net60 for pilot + temporary invoice ladder

Oliver — thanks for the clear ask and the VAT details. Short answer: we can be flexible for pilot customers, but need to balance exposure with approvals. Proposed approach below:

- Option A (preferred): Net45 payment terms with a 25% deposit for month 1. Redwood to provide EU VAT-compliant invoices (we will show your VAT ID and indicate reverse-charge where applicable).
- Option B (conditional): Net60 for first three invoices, contingent on an approved credit application and a provisional credit cap (suggested €300,000) plus a PO confirming the ladder.

Action items for Acme to speed approval:
1) Complete & return the credit application (PDF).
2) Send a PO referencing "pilot ladder" and the invoice schedule you prefer (we can template).
3) Confirm billing legal entity and VAT ID for invoice header.

On our side I’ll loop in Finance for a quick credit check. If credit checks are clean we can sign off on Option B and produce VAT-line items as requested. If not, Option A gets you immediate onboarding with Net45 + deposit.

Ben / Monica — can you run a provisional limit and confirm how fast we can turn an EU VAT invoice once entity details are confirmed?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Hi Oliver — attaching the standard credit application and our VAT notice for EU customers.

Attachments: Acme_credit_application_20261130.pdf, Redwood_W9_and_vat_notice.pdf

A few clarifications from Finance:
- We can provisionally agree to a "staggered invoice ladder" (we typically split invoices into Pilot / Post-pilot-1 / Post-pilot-2). For each invoice we need the PO number and the billing entity.
- Provisional credit caps are usually set after a quick bureau + trade reference check — expect 48 business hours after we receive the completed application.
- If you need Net60 across the board we will ask for either an increased deposit (30–40%) or a letter of credit.

I'll run the paperwork through and ping you with an internal provisional cap estimate.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Request: move to Net60 for pilot + temporary invoice ladder

Thanks Marcus / Monica — we've completed the credit application and returned it to Monica this morning (see attached in our outbound mail). A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- VAT: Acme confirms reverse-charge applies. Please make sure the invoice line items include VAT ID fields and a note "VAT reverse-charge: customer responsible" so our AP team can process automatically.
- PO: Elena will issue a PO today referencing the proposed ladder (Pilot / Month+1 / Month+2). Will that suffice for your billing team?
- Exposures: Acme cannot do upfront letters of credit for a pilot, so Net45 + 25% deposit would be our fallback if cap can't be increased quickly.

Appreciate the quick turnaround; we want to start the pilot in the first week of January.

Best,
Oliver

Subject: Final: provisional credit cap and invoice schedule (DEAL-8347)

Oliver / Marcus — finance completed the provisional review. Summary below and next steps: 

- Provisional credit cap: €275,000 (subject to final trade verification and standard T&Cs).
- Agreed billing cadence for pilot: three invoices (Pilot, Post-pilot 1, Post-pilot 2).
- Terms: Net45 with a 25% deposit on the Pilot invoice. If Acme supplies a corporate guarantee or higher deposit, we can convert to Net60 for the ladder.
- VAT: Redwood will issue EU VAT-detailed invoices showing your VAT ID and a reverse-charge note. That will satisfy Acme AP per our tax counsel.

Next steps:
1) Oliver / Elena to upload PO referencing DEAL-8347 and the ladder schedule.
2) Acme to e-sign the attached credit agreement (DocuSign link below) to finalize the provisional cap and payment terms.
3) Once signed, Marcus will trigger onboarding and issue the first VAT-compliant invoice.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/ENVELOPEID/ABCD-8347
Attachment: Credit_Agreement_SIGN_ME_8347.docx

If there are urgency constraints for the January start, we can provision the account on Net45 immediately upon receipt of the deposit and PO.
